correctness.rationale: A polynomial harmonic vanishing on a hyperplane has zero even normal Taylor coefficients by the Laplace recurrence and is reflection-odd. Two reflections generate rotation by 2theta; an irrational rotation precludes a nonzero odd finite Fourier polynomial, while reduced rational angle p/q permits sine frequencies divisible by q. Equivariant Fischer decomposition removes radial-square factors and gives multiplicity binom(ell-m+d-3,d-3) in each sine m-sector. On ker R0, a fixed injective trace map composed with diagonal sin(mtheta) controls the second observation, and the complementary component is coercive under R0: min-max gives precisely N quadratically vanishing Gram eigenvalues; analyticity yields determinant order 2N. The explicit harmonic Im(x1+ix2)^m has Rayleigh ratio c_{d,m}sin²(mtheta) with c_{d,m}<=d/[2(d-1)], and Dirichlet approximation furnishes the stated 1/L² upper bound. Limits: fixed ell near resonance; no infinite-degree uniform stability. Independent finite dimension/multiplicity checks corroborate but do not prove the theorem.

originality.rationale: The 2017 Anghel root-of-unity criterion concerns bivariate harmonic divisibility by a conic and is the closest rational-angle algebraic precursor: it does not yield the ambient-d>=4 full harmonic-mode multiplicities or quadratic vanishing order of a two-equator Gram determinant. Existing low-degree continuous two-equator spectra cover ell=2 or 3 only; they cannot dominate all ell. General Fischer/dihedral arguments and angular sine decomposition are standard inputs, not new achievements. The original claim of all-degree nullity+detuning is not demonstrably implied by the inspected primary comparisons, though an equivalent unindexed multidimensional theorem remains a risk.

value.rationale: A pair of intersecting codimension-one equators is a canonical minimal multi-view continuous observation geometry. The theorem classifies all resonance angles and exact nullspace dimensions at every degree, proves a quantitative quadratic conditioning law near resonance, and separates pointwise injectivity from high-degree uniform stability. These are motivated structural boundaries for harmonic recovery rather than a chosen finite census.
